You body is in a constant state of death and renewal - cells die and are replaced by new ones. When someone, say, breaks a bone beyond repair, doctors can use cadaver bone to replace the shattered bone. (Allografting - it's kinda cool.) After so many years, all of the old cells are replaced and the bone is, essentially, the receivers bone. The body knows what to do - it recognizes the dying cells and replaces them with new cells of its own making.

Now, this is bone. Squishier stuff like organs, veins, etc. regenerate a lot faster because of their nature (not a lot, but a bit more.) A uterus wouldn't be the donor's uterus after awhile, it would be the receivers uterus. And any babies made in the womb would be fed from the mother's blood, cells, whatever - so no, it wouldn't be like adoption. It would be hers.
